rv.q: With two thoroughly committed stars as Macbeth and his Lady, and a conductor with a penchant for high-octane drama, the show lent fresh tension and heart-stopping insight to a popular opera and its even more popular source material.
I'd be happy to see it again—certainly with as good a cast as was mustered for the gala opening.
Nézet-Séguin led a richly detailed, passion-fueled account of the score.
Its urgent rhythms, galloping pace and driving energy are well displayed in this production, directed by Karolina Sofulak and conducted by rising star Nil Venditti.

A consistently involving and powerful production by debuting Louisa Proske served Verdi, Piave/Maffei, and Shakespeare and proved a rousing success crowned by a towering performance of the title role by baritone Quinn Kelsey!
Ultimately however, the result proved to be a mixed bag with one of its leading roles delivered with incredible passion and the other utterly lacking in it.

cn.t: Critics praise Louisa Proske's gripping Met Opera debut production of Verdi's "Macbeth," highlighting thoroughly committed star performances from Quinn Kelsey and Lise Davidsen, along with the production's intense energy and theatrical power.
